description: RELATIONS-A. The measurement-system facts Python needs to compare two figures written in different measures, and to read a percentage of a figure. Nothing here names a domain, a quantity or a language: `prefixes` are the decimal prefixes of the SI (BIPM), written as their symbols, and `dimensionless_scales` are symbols that stand for a pure number of a fixed size (the percent sign is one hundredth). A unit token is read as a prefix and a base only when both figures being compared write units that differ by exactly such a prefix on the same base, so `mL` against `L` converts and `kg` against `box` does not. A unit written with a digit or a caret (`m2`, `m^2`) is never converted, because the unit reader drops the exponent. `bases` are the SI base and coherent derived unit symbols, plus the litre, that a prefix may stand before; a token is read as a prefix and a base only when that base is declared here, so `ha` against `a`, `dB` against `B`, `min` against `in` and `cd` against `d` are never converted (D-198). The operator may add a prefix, a base or a scale here; removing one stops that conversion and the comparison is refused on the pairing map instead.
